items.sourceText:
## New Features

- Save reusable prompts and slash commands in ten numbered `/presets` slots, with a keyboard menu for quick access. (#54380, #54381)
- Set model, reasoning effort, speed, and permission profiles directly with inline `/model` and `/permissions` arguments. (#54378, #54383)
- Preview viewed and generated images in the fullscreen transcript on terminals supporting Kitty or Sixel graphics. (#54216)
- Authenticate enterprise MCP connections using eligible Codex account grants or dedicated sign-in, including OAuth clients requiring secrets. (#55334, #55859, #56001)
- Mask credentials during supported remote Bash commands and Zsh snapshot sessions, including credentials from custom providers. (#54309, #54432, #56049)
- The Amazon Bedrock setup wizard is now enabled by default, with API key entry grouped alongside other AWS sign-in methods when credentials are detected. (#56033, #56023)

## Bug Fixes

- Failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries in conversation history, and background compaction failures fall back without panicking. (#53932, #55581)
- Resuming sessions now finds compressed histories and restores saved thread settings instead of replacing them with global defaults. (#54008, #55923)
- Windows HTTPS and WebSocket connections now handle proxy authentication challenges using the signed-in user’s Negotiate or NTLM credentials. (#55994, #56000)
- CLI configuration overrides are preserved when `-c` or `--config` appears at multiple subcommand levels. (#56022)
- Queued prompts now wait for pending permission selections to resolve before continuing. (#55682)
- Hardened sandbox checks for case-variant metadata paths on macOS and replaceable symlinks used to locate executables. (#54273, #55384)

## Chores

- Reduced disk usage by pruning unused installations, cleaning abandoned marketplace checkouts, and bounding daemon logs. (#53827, #55149, #55689, #55690, #55856)
- Updated the embedded JavaScript runtime with safety checks for optimized `Array.sort` operations. (#54519)

( #56033 , #56023 ) Bug Fixes Failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries in conversation history, and background compaction failures fall back without panicking. ( #54008 , #55923 ) Windows HTTPS and WebSocket connections now handle proxy authentication challenges using the signed-in user’s Negotiate or NTLM credentials. ( #55994 , #56000 ) CLI configuration overrides are preserved when -c or --config appears at multiple subcommand levels. ( #55682 ) Hardened sandbox checks for case-variant metadata paths on macOS and replaceable symlinks used to locate executables. # Hermes Agent v0.22.5

**Release Date:** October 22, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~81 PRs merged since v0.22.4 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.23.0.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## About this release

Measured at commit `bf0203a794a`, the window since v0.22.4 contains **231 non-merge commits** across **804 changed files** (+35,212 / −17,885), **81 merged PRs** and **30 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: Nous sign-in reworked (every sign-in is the plain device login, the free-tier guest hands over to your account, the result shows who signed in, connectors offer sign-in instead of opening a guest), `hermes update` holding back a stable release it refuses instead of offering it, Windows `hermes update` no longer stuck on the old launcher after a Python repin, usage-window plan support (plan gauges, limit cards and model-switch recovery for window-based plans), pluggable delegation backends (route subagents by model map or profile, switchable per session), plugin slash commands that can ask you to pick an option, `hermes import-agent`, OpenClaw migration, `hermes mcp serve` and the Singularity backend moving out of core into plugins (setup offers the importer when it finds another agent), Desktop drag-to-pin in the sidebar and one-click plugin installs with tier badges, the Electron 44 upgrade, Pillow 13 and a batch of dependency security bumps, a clear message when a chat's working folder is gone, `hermes update` recovering paused gateways after a damaged `.git`, long Claude DirectSDK answers no longer cut off by the stall timer, Desktop group chats showing which bot is working again, and the experimental webhook-mode MCP events client.

**Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.23.0**, which will document everything from v0.22.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.22.4...v0.22.5](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.22.4...v0.22.5)

items.sourceText: # ChatGPT for iOS ### New features - View and stop background commands using the new pill above the composer on supported remote hosts. - Mention chats from other connected hosts with `@`. ### Improvements and bug fixes - A loading indicator now shows when saved messages are refreshing. - Activity groups are cleaner, and you can open images inspected by Codex on demand. - Unanswered questions remain available after a turn finishes and when reopening a chat. - More reliable replies to questions while another prompt is starting or finishing. - Autocomplete suggestions appear as each source loads, without waiting for slower sources. - Usage-limit explanations and reset times now appear directly in the chat. - Fixed prompts incorrectly appearing to fail after a response timeout. - Fixed extra lines in diffs after repeated edits to the same file. - Images in responses open in the full-screen gallery, and attachment removal targets the correct image. - The voice button returns after a call ends, so you can start another without reopening the chat.

# Hermes Agent v0.22.4

**Release Date:** October 21, 2026

> Patch release. Desktop stops showing suggestion pills above the composer, plus small plugin and dashboard fixes, for the CLI and installer, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## Fixes

- **Desktop no longer shows suggestion pills above the composer.** The pills appeared for no clear reason, mostly nudging you to set up MCP servers. They and the helpers that only they used are gone. ([#142559](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142559))
- **Plugins that install nothing skip the dependency consent step.** A plugin that declares no dependencies, or whose `pyproject.toml` installs nothing, now enables without an empty consent prompt. ([#142569](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142569))
- **Dashboard: WhatsApp can be safely re-paired after logging out.** ([#142439](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142439))
- **Desktop plugin review:** the surface lint no longer flags prototype writes; reviewers check them by hand. ([#142586](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142586))
- **Desktop: the approval-mode chip follows the active profile's mode.** ([#142565](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142565))
- **Release builds:** the desktop bundle's pre-build check gets enough time to verify archived build inputs when storage is slow. ([#142623](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142623))

Also new in the plugin catalog: bubblewrap (bwrap terminal backend on Linux), Singularity/Apptainer, mcp-serve (Hermes as an MCP server), agent-importers (`hermes import-agent`, now with Cursor), inbox and workflow-record from Hermes Labs. Telegram Business moves to the Hermes Labs community tier.

## About this release

Measured at commit `4d04303818b`, the window since v0.22.3 contains **14 non-merge commits** across **82 changed files** (+1,475 / −3,022) and **13 merged PRs**.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.22.3...v0.22.4](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.22.3...v0.22.4)

## @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything 2.0.0

* Release v2.0.0: merge v2/main into main by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5166

## Python servers: changes for clients

`mcp-server-fetch`, `mcp-server-git` and `mcp-server-time` have no CHANGELOG, so here is what changes for a client in `2026.10.19`. They are now built on the MCP Python SDK's high-level `MCPServer` ([#5175](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5175)).

- **Unknown tool:** a JSON-RPC `-32602` error (`Unknown tool: <name>`) in both protocol eras, as the spec requires. It used to be an `isError` result.
- **Tool errors** read `Error executing tool <name>: <message>`. Argument-validation errors now use pydantic's wording. Both are still `isError` results.
- **Capabilities:** each server now advertises `prompts` and `resources` capabilities (with `listChanged: false`). fetch's `fetch` prompt is the only entry in those lists.
- **time:** `get_current_time` and `convert_time` declare an `outputSchema` and return `structuredContent`. The text content is unchanged.
- **fetch:** a `prompts/get` result's `description` is now always the prompt's registered description.
- **Requires** `mcp>=2.3,<3`.

## mcp-server-fetch 2026.10.19

### What's Changed

* Port fetch, git and time to the MCP Python SDK v2 by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5062

* chore: stamp Python CalVer versions for 2026.10.19 by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5177
* Release v2.0.0: merge v2/main into main by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5166

## mcp-server-git 2026.10.19

### What's Changed

* Port fetch, git and time to the MCP Python SDK v2 by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5062

items.sourceText:
## New Features

- Open `/config` to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. (#52990, #53429)
- Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. (#51812, #51835)
- Configure a leader key in `/keymap`. The default is `Ctrl+X`, shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to `F9`. (#52273)
- Restart a managed background server from `/daemon`. Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. (#53173)
- Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. (#52245)
- Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. `codex exec` can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. (#53701, #53717)

## Bug Fixes

- Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. (#53150, #53419, #53424)
- The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate `Host` headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. (#51650, #52661, #53506)
- Return to an existing side conversation with `/side` after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. (#52184, #53436)
- On Windows, `Ctrl+V` and `Shift+Insert` paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. (#53224, #52967, #53453)
- Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. (#52652, #53331, #53622)
- `codex exec` no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. (#53444)

## Documentation

- Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. (#51768)
- Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. (#52610)

## Chores

- Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched `zsh`. Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. (#52160, #52213)
- Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. (#52178)

( #52990 , #53429 ) Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. items.sourceText: # GPT-5.5 retirement in Codex Effective October 14, 2026, at noon PDT (19:00 UTC), GPT-5.5 retires from Codex for users signed in with ChatGPT. The OpenAI API and Codex sessions authenticated with an API key aren't affected. Use **GPT-6.1 Sol** (`gpt-6.1-sol`) when available to your plan and client. Update workspace defaults, saved model settings, managed configurations, custom agents, scheduled tasks, and scripts that still select `gpt-5.5`. See [GPT-5.5 retirement](/codex/models#gpt-55-retirement) for plan-specific replacements and [workspace model availability](/codex/enterprise/workspace-model-availability#prepare-for-the-gpt-55-retirement) for administrator guidance.
